title: Illumina library prep
subtitle: From genomic DNA to a sequencer-ready library, one step at a time.
objectives: Draw and label a finished Illumina library molecule.
Explain what each prep step does and why it is needed.
Name the main ways protocols differ and what each choice changes.
Recognise common library-prep failures from their QC signatures.

steps.title: Starting material
steps.caption: We start with high-molecular-weight genomic DNA from the sample.

steps.title: Input QC
steps.caption: Before anything else: how much DNA, how intact, how clean?

steps.title: Fragmentation
steps.caption: DNA is sheared into fragments near the target insert size.

steps.title: End repair
steps.caption: Shearing leaves messy ends; enzymes trim or fill them to blunt, phosphorylated ends.

steps.title: A-tailing
steps.caption: A single A on each 3′ end lets adapters with a T overhang ligate, and stops fragments ligating to each other.

steps.title: Adapter ligation
steps.caption: Adapters carry everything the sequencer needs: flow-cell binding sites, primer sites and indexes.

steps.title: Bead clean-up / size selection
steps.caption: Magnetic beads remove leftover adapters and fragments that are too short or too long. The bead ratio sets the cut-off.

steps.title: Library PCR
steps.caption: PCR completes or enriches full-length molecules and raises the yield. Each cycle adds bias.

steps.title: Library QC
steps.caption: Check the size distribution and measure molarity by qPCR, which counts only molecules that can actually be sequenced.

steps.title: Pool, normalise, load
steps.caption: Libraries are pooled in equal amounts, denatured and loaded onto the flow cell.
